Content:
How much bigger is the size of the digit [MATH: {\color{blue}9}] in [MATH: 3.{\color{blue}9}6] than the size of the digit [MATH: {\color{red}9}] in [MATH: 4.3{\color{red}9}?]

Content:
Let's start by writing down the place values for [MATH: 3.{\color{blue}9}6.] We see that the [MATH: \color{blue}9] is in the tenths place.

Content:
| ones | | tenths | hundredths |

Content:
Now, we write the place values for [MATH: 4.3{\color{red}9}.] Here, the [MATH: \color{red}9] is in the hundredths place.

| ones | | tenths | hundredths |
| [MATH: 4] | . | [MATH: 3] | [MATH: \color{red}9] |

Content:
To compare the two digits, we move one step to the left in the place value chart. Each step to the left is an increase by a factor of [MATH: 10]:

Content:
| ones | | tenths | hundredths |
| | . | [MATH: \color{blue}9] | [MATH: \color{red}9] |
| [IMG: /graphics/49d3467ab7b1bd12ecb1afbcab92218b] |

Content:
Therefore, the value of the digit [MATH: \color{blue}9] in the tenths place is [MATH: 10] times greater than the value of the digit [MATH: \color{red}9] in the hundredths place.
